description.narrative: The main objective of the Project is to remove a constraint to sustainable economic growth that will help to increase standards of living and to reduce poverty in the project area. This will be achieved by providing affordable railway transportation in the unserved, less developed areas to create conditions necessary for developing local resources and generating employment and income enhancing opportunities. The Project comprises: (i) constructing 520 kms double track electrified standard gauge Class I railway between Taiyuan and Dingbian, 232 kms single track from Dingbian-Zhongwei, and 192 kms single track from Dingbian to Yinchuan, (ii) constructing 41 new railway stations complete with facilities, (iii) a safety component which includes providing modern technology and equipment for management information system, operational safety equipment, and mechanized maintenance of track, and capacity building of staff including training, (iv) e-governance and management information system (MIS), (v) providing training on the use and maintenance of the modern equipment, (vi) land acquisition and resettlement, (vii) protecting the environment and mitigating adverse environmental effects, (viii) providing consulting services for construction supervision, monitoring and evaluation, marketing and business development, and (ix) strengthening institutional capabilities.

No accident had happened since the start of trial operation. The operation of TZY is assigned to Taiyuan, Lanzhou, and Xian Railway Administrations. The ADB loan review mission in December 2012 took the train on a section of the railway and noted that the passenger and freight operations are undertaken in smooth and normal manner and the railway stations are functioning well. Output: Railway infrastructure and associated facilities improved along the Taiyuan-Zhongwei railway corridor. Indicator: Environment at the project site is protected and adverse environmental impacts minimized by implementing mitigation measures as included in the EIA and SEIA Mitigation measures included in civil works contracts. Progress/Status: The Engineering Management Unit coordinates the environment management under the TZYRC and supervises contractors for their compliance with environment management as required in the environment management plan (EMP). Two environment engineers are staffed in the unit. All contractors also set up responsible unit or office to look after the environment management. The TZYRC has set up environment management rules and procedures and mainstreams them in the project implementation. Beijing OASIS is engaged as the external environment monitor to oversee the EMP implementation as well as the monitoring program. The Yellow River Soil and Water Conservation Monitoring Center is engaged to monitor soil erosion induced by construction activities along the alignment. The Xi'an Yellow River Engineering Supervision Company is engaged to supervise the implementation of soil erosion control plan.
The ADB loan review mission in Decemer 2012 acknowledged that the completion technical review (CTR) for soil erosion protection plan (SEPP) has been conducted. It was reported that disposal sites have been properly protected and restoration of temporarily acquired land is well undertaken, wastewater treatment facilities have been installed in the new railway stations. It is noted that facilities for utilizing solar energy have been installed in 29 locations. The SEPP acceptance approval is expected to be achieved in the first half of 2013. The initial CTR for environmental management plan (EMP) is ongoing. The main outstanding issues discovered are (i) the sound barrier and sound-insulating windows that have been constructed are less than what is required in the EIA; and (ii) additional measures need to be taken for desulfurization in 14 boilers coal-fired boilers in 10 stations. TZYRC is required to pay close attention to these issues and resolve them by the end of the first half of 2013, and complete the preparation for EIA acceptance approval as early as possible. Beijing OASIS, the environmental monitoring agency, is required to closely follow up. Data Source: Environmental monitoring reports, PAMs, and PCR Baseline year: 2006 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2006 Baseline value: N Target year: 2012 Target value: Y
